newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu wants Zaire talks held close to home.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu wants Zaire talks held close to home.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko will not travel to South Africa this week for a much expected meeting with rebel leader Laurent Kabila on ending Zaire's civil war, his son and spokesman said on Monday.
"Apparently President Mobutu doesn't want to travel to South Africa. He prefers somewhere else," Nzanga Mobutu told Reuters. "It's a long flight and he's still convalescing."
Mobutu, 66, had prostate cancer surgery in August and is still receiving treatment, although he looked in fair shape at his last public appearance a few days ago.

Some regional analysts said health may not be the only reason for Mobutu's reluctance to go to South Africa. One said President Nelson Mandela's mediation was perceived by some members of the Kinshasa government as an international public relations exercise for South Africa.

South Africa has staged a series of exploratory talks involving envoys of the two camps. Mandela last week met Kabila and official South African sources said later a Mobutu-Kabila meeting could take place in South Africa this week.
Mobutu's opponents have also threatened that if he ventures far afield his return will be blocked.
Asked if his father would prefer to go to Brazzaville, capital of Congo across the river from Kinshasa, Nzanga said: "From what I've heard Kabila doesn't want to go to Brazzaville."
Congo's President Pascal Lissouba is pursuing parallel efforts to bring Zaire's chief protagonists to the negotiating table in his country. He met Mobutu in Kinshasa last week.

Benin's President Mathieu Kerekou was expected in the Zaire capital on Sunday for talks with Mobutu presumed to be linked to the attempts to end the civil war through diplomacy. His trip was cancelled at the last minute but officials in Kinshasa said he was still expected this week.
Mobutu's Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda has been touring regional capitals since last week.
Nzanga said the Mobutu-Kabila talks were not off and that negotiators from both sides were working on a date and venue.
Mobutu reluctantly agreed to meet Kabila, who demanded direct talks as a condition for ending his six-month-old armed campaign to topple the long-serving president.

Kabila's forces have seized more than half of Zaire's vast territory and are threatening to bring the war to the capital Kinshasa if Mobutu does not agree to step down at their planned meeting. Mobutu wants the talks to set the stage for elections.
Diplomats and military analysts in the Zaire capital are skeptical about Kabila's genuine interest in the talks given his overwhelming military advantage on the ground.
The rebel leader reinforced such doubts at the weekend by declaring that he expects the planned meeting to be a formal handover of power by Mobutu, who has been in power since 1965.
